Both sides deliver the same thing: extra rules text riding on the base impulse's own entry, no number. The three option names and their element restrictions match the printed list one-for-one.

The registry is display-only (header comment, situationalBonuses.ts:11), which is the same conditional-note treatment their text-qualified bonus gets.

Read public/core.json classes['champion'].subclass directly: 7 options (Desecration, Grandeur, Iniquity, Justice, Liberation, Obedience, Redemption) matching the 7 printed causes, each with a featureIds grant for the reaction plus the relentless/exalted upgrade text. Same count, same names, same delivered reaction.

The packet's ourFields omitted grantedStrikes — read public/core.json directly. Die, damage type, group and all four traits match the printed strike exactly, which is what their item grant delivers. We additionally model the unarmored requirement and the Speed bonus they do not encode; nothing they deliver is missing on our side.

Compared all three deliverables. Both trained skills match. Tradition (arcane) and at-will are carried by the cantrip-grant lane. Same count, same spells, same tradition.

The third clause (one fewer free hand to Climb or Trip) is prose on both sides — they encode nothing for it, we carry it as a record note. Nothing they deliver is absent here.
